title: Young Hall floor 4

source.what: "Fourth Floor Plan" from the architects' UCLA Young Hall chemistry lab feasibility study: full floor with walls, corridors, stairs, elevators, restrooms and the bridge to the adjacent building; the project area is shaded; no room numbers, no scale bar
source.license: architect's portfolio image, copyright Paul Murdoch Architects; used here only to trace wall positions

how: Architects' plan with no scale bar. The plan's long bar runs top to bottom, so it is turned 90 degrees (north is to the plan's left); with the rotation fixed, a scale sweep of the footprint against the building outline is best at 10.5 cm/px (median 1.05 m, 90% within 4.7 m). Orientation check: the floor 2 trace's elevator, stair and two restrooms land within 5 to 30 px (0.5 to 3 m) of the same cores on this plan. Four synthetic control points carry that transform.
notes: Architects' feasibility-study plan (2019): no room numbers and no scale bar, so rooms are traced without numbers; stairs, elevators and restrooms labeled by hand from the plan's own callouts. The 'PROJECT AREA 8,850 GSF' shading is the study's lab area, not a room.

Georeference: the plan is drawn with north to the left; it is turned 90 degrees and scaled by a sweep of the footprint against the building outline (best 10.5 cm/px, median 1.05 m). Orientation check: the floor 2 trace's elevator, stair and two restrooms land within 0.5 to 3 m of the same cores on this plan.
Hand cuts seal the two restroom doors off the junction lobby.
